title: Language-model safety probes transferred despite shifts in learned directions
summary: Across four language-model families, the directions fitted to separate benign and harmful requests shifted by about 17° to 35° after distillation or instruction tuning. Applying the base probes unchanged shifted AUC by −0.011 to +0.027 on XSTest and −0.015 to +0.053 on an independent prompt set.
ai_technology: Fitted linear activation probes; Qwen2.5, Llama 3.1 and distilled DeepSeek-R1 variants

evidence.tested: Linear classifiers trained on the four base models were evaluated unchanged on two matched successors per family. Transfer was compared with the same probe’s performance on the base model.
evidence.unknown: Similar observed accuracy does not establish equivalence, and XSTest fold intervals are too narrow. On OR-Bench the probes flagged 29% to 42% of benign prompts that sounded harmful.
evidence.ai_role: Fitted activation classifiers estimated directions and classification performance on base and successor models. Their transfer separated change in direction from change in discrimination.
